description: Put an uploaded audio clip on a video asset's own timeline track, so music or narration can be re-levelled in the AR editor instead of being baked into the uploaded file. Re-renders the asset as a new active revision and keeps the previous cut as a revision. Upload the clip with upload_publisher_audio first. Note the rendered file is always a flat mixdown — AR has no output with separate streams; the track lives in the editor's saved timeline.

asset_id.description: Video asset id, e.g. from upload_publisher_video.

audio_clip_volume.description: Clip level, 0-200 percent, 100 being unity. Default 100. A music bed under speech usually wants 60-80.

audio_duration_s.description: Length of the audio clip in seconds, when it differs from the video. Defaults to the video length.

audio_position_s.description: Where the clip starts on the video's timeline, in seconds. Default 0.

audio_track_label.description: Track name shown in the editor, e.g. 'Music' or 'Voiceover'. Default 'Music'.

notification_message.description: Short user-facing sentence for this action if the follow-up reply fails. Plain text only; do not mention template syntax or variable names.

publisher_pid.description: Project id from list_projects or create_project.

source_media_url.description: Optional. The cut to re-render from: the one before this audio was mixed in. Leave it out and AR resolves and records it. Set it only when you know better, e.g. re-pointing an asset at a different silent master.

video_base_volume.description: Level of the video's own sound, 0-1. Default 1.0. NOTE: exactly 1.0 makes ffmpeg's amix divide by the input count, so video and music both land about 6 dB down; any other value pins both to the levels asked for. Nothing limits the sum, so leave headroom (e.g. 0.75 with a clip at 70) rather than summing two loud sources.

video_duration_s.description: Length of the video in seconds. The editor needs it to lay out the timeline.

name: set_publisher_video_audio
